Subject: PrivDeploy evidence pathway + witnessing windows

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the call today. As discussed, our legal team needs a concrete, auditable path for (1) limited operator witness access to the on‑prem appliance during initial commissioning; (2) evidence transfer for snapshots used in validation; and (3) a concise list of what Redwood will and will not retain (logs, KV snapshots, backups).

Specific asks to unblock our MSA redlines: 
- A short playbook describing the witness procedure (who attends, duration, read‑only controls, credential handback).
- A witness schedule window (two 2‑hour windows next week) so our security team can plan.
- Clarify license scope for bundled models vs. customer data residency in Section 4.2 (we flagged operator custody language).
- Any existing attestation templates or prior SOC‑style exhibits you can share.

Appreciate a short turn on this (we need to surface to legal by EOD Thu).

Regards,
Emily Cox
Director of Security & Compliance
Acme Health

Hi Emily —

Thanks — I pulled together an initial playbook and a proposed witness window. Drafts attached. High level points up front:

- Witnessing: Redwood does not take custody of customer data. We can provide a supervised, read‑only witness session for up to two engineers during commissioning. Access is via ephemeral console access that expires at session end; we will record session metadata (who, start/end, actions) and hand over logs.
- Snapshots: We can provide a signed hash of the snapshot and a signed manifest describing the snapshot contents. We will not deposit customer snapshots into an escrow repository; instead we provide cryptographic proof and an escorted data‑transfer process.
- License scope: Operator runtime and model binaries that Redwood ships under the Order Form are licensed for use in the customer environment; customer data and any customer‑trained fine‑tuning artifacts remain customer property. We flagged language for Section 4.2 that clarifies that operator diagnostics are limited to non‑PII telemetry unless otherwise agreed.

Attached: privdeploy_evidence_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook draft) and a marked redlines file.

Proposed witness windows: Tue 2026‑09‑14 14:00–16:00 PDT OR Wed 2026‑09‑15 09:00–11:00 PDT. Let me know which works for your team and I’ll schedule and send an ICS.

Cc'ing Karthik and Marissa to confirm legal/ops wording and to capture any required attestation templates.

Best,

Team —

I reviewed Rachel's draft playbook and marked a few legal adjustments. Key suggested redlines: 

1) Witness access: replace any phrasing that could be read as Redwood "taking custody" with "supervised witnessing" and an explicit line that customer retains exclusive control over keys and snapshot artifacts.
2) Snapshot proof: replace 'signed snapshot transfer' wording with 'signed snapshot manifest and HSM‑backed hash verification' — keeps us from being asked to escrow actual data.
3) Audit evidence: propose a 90‑day retention carveout for session metadata in our logs (for troubleshooting and security review), and a standard procedure for providing exports on request with a signed NDA.

Marissa — can you confirm whether we have an attestation template for witnessing that is DR‑neutral? Hannah — inventory of any prior SOC‑like exhibits would help (we may attach a redacted evidence binder).

I also propose we include a short 'failure mode' clause for the commissioning window: if the witness session reveals a material inability to validate operator controls, Redwood will provide a remediation plan and an agreed mitigation timeline, not an automatic transfer of operator software.

I'll attach inline comments to the redlines_marked.docx.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
